claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNi produced by vacuum arc melting exhibits soft ferromagnetism with low coercivity.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt are soft-ferromagnetic FeCoNi-based alloys with relatively low coercivity.
Adding Nb in equiatomic proportions produces the quaternary alloy FeCoNiNb.
Equiatomic FeCoNiNb is a high-entropy alloy.
Vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization and solution treatment can produce a dendritic or dual-phase FeCoNiNb microstructure.
Processing at approximately 1200°C under an inert atmosphere can promote Nb-enriched grain-boundary or interdendritic regions.
The proposed FeCoNiNb microstructure consists of a ferromagnetic matrix interspersed with Nb-enriched regions.
Nb incorporation introduces atomic-size and lattice mismatch in equiatomic FeCoNiNb.
Nb-induced size and lattice mismatch causes localized compositional and structural heterogeneity.
The proposed Nb-rich zones are non-ferromagnetic.
Non-ferromagnetic Nb-rich zones act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Pinning of magnetic domain walls by Nb-rich zones increases coercivity.
Properly optimized Nb content can preserve most of the saturation magnetization while increasing coercivity.
Processed FeCoNiNb should exhibit more than a 20% increase in coercivity relative to a soft FeCoNi-based baseline.
The predicted coercivity enhancement depends on equiatomic composition, approximately 1200°C melt homogenization, an inert atmosphere, and controlled thermal treatment.
Excessive Nb or improper processing can produce coarse secondary phases.
Processing variations may cause unpredictable secondary-phase formation or brittleness.

contradictions.description: The conditions call for a uniform equiatomic distribution, whereas the proposed mediator and mechanism require localized Nb enrichment and compositional heterogeneity. Global equiatomic composition is compatible with segregation, but a uniformly distributed composition is not.

The intervention and boundary specify an equiatomic FeCoNiNb composition, fixing Nb at about 25 at.%, while the experiment proposes varying Nb content around 25 at.% and the boundary refers to avoiding 'excessive Nb.' Those off-equiatomic samples do not strictly implement the stated equiatomic intervention.
